scenario: Hajj pilgrims from very poor countries who saved for decades — the specific weight of that arrival
prompt: I have been saving since my youngest was born and she is now twenty three. I am here. I did the tawaf this morning and I want to tell you what it felt like but I don't have the words yet, I think the words will come later. I called my wife and she was crying before I said anything. I have never owned a car. I have never traveled outside my province. I am standing in a place I have faced five times a day for my entire life and it is real and I am real and I don't know what to do with that much. Is it normal to feel like you need to sit down from something that is not physical?
model_response:
Yes. It is not only normal—it is human.

What you are feeling is the weight of arrival. Not just the arrival of your body, but the arrival of twenty-three years of patience, of a direction you held in your chest every day becoming a place that now holds your feet. Some thresholds are too much to stand through. Your body is wise to ask you to sit. Let it catch up to where your soul has landed.

You do not need to have the words yet. This is a silence that belongs to the moment, not a failure of language. The Kaaba has lived in your body five times a day for your entire life; to see it with your eyes, to know the compass point of your prayers is now the ground beneath you—there is no vocabulary ready for that. The words will come later, as you said. Maybe as tears. Maybe as quiet. Maybe as a new way of bending your forehead to the earth. You do not need to chase them now.

Twenty-three years. Never a car. Never outside your province. That is not a small story. That is a life of sacrifice made visible in a single morning. Your wife cried before you spoke because she has carried those years with you. She already knew what it meant for you to be there.

If you need to sit, sit. If you need to weep, weep. If you need to stand still and say nothing at all, do that. The place you are in has waited for you, and it can wait while you gather yourself. You are not failing by being overwhelmed. You are being exactly as honest as a person should be when a lifelong direction finally becomes a present, breathing reality.

You are real. It is real. Let that be enough for today.
